root_cause.text: The netfilter nft_bitwise shift initialization failed to validate a zero shift operand, allowing nft_bitwise left/right shift code to execute carry propagation with `BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift`, which becomes an undefined 32-bit shift on `u32`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `nft_bitwise_init_shift()` from rejecting only `priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)` to also reject `!priv->data.data[0]`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that a zero shift makes `BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift` evaluate to 32, causing undefined behaviour.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject zero and oversized shift amounts during nft bitwise shift initialization by returning `-EINVAL` and releasing the parsed data.
intent_record.what: The condition validating `priv->data.data[0]` in `nft_bitwise_init_shift()` was expanded from checking only `priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)` to also reject `!priv->data.data[0]`, making zero an invalid shift value alongside values greater than or equal to the u32 bit width.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes initialization of a bitwise shift expression to fail with `-EINVAL` when the shift amount is zero, in addition to already rejecting oversized shift amounts, and it releases the associated data before returning.

candidates.rationale: This validation only rejects oversized shift amounts but fails to reject a zero shift operand. As a result, zero is accepted and later execution can evaluate BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift with shift==0, leading to an undefined 32-bit shift in carry propagation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This initialization-time validation is incomplete: it rejects only shift amounts greater than or equal to the u32 bit width, but it does not reject a zero shift operand. That allows shift==0 to reach later left/right shift execution, where carry propagation computes BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift and then performs an undefined 32-bit shift on u32.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant shift-validation logic is fully visible in `nft_bitwise_init_shift()`, so the snippet is sufficient to judge this commit version. The root cause requires failure to reject a zero shift operand. In this commit, the only validation after parsing is `if (priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)) { ... return -EINVAL; }`. This rejects values `>= 32` but still allows `0`, because `0 >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)` is false. Therefore the vulnerable condition (zero shift accepted) is present in this function. The commit does add upfront type/length validation via `struct nft_data_desc desc = { .type = NFT_DATA_VALUE, .size = sizeof(priv->data), .len = sizeof(u32), };` and `err = nft_data_init(NULL, &priv->data, &desc, tb[NFTA_BITWISE_DATA]);`, but that only ensures the operand is a 32-bit value; it does not add the missing nonzero check. Since the fix for this vulnerability would require rejecting zero as well (for example `== 0 || >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)` or similar), the fix is not present here.
